evidence.q1: Hero fills roughly the top 85% of the first viewport: eyebrow 'SUMMER 2026 - AGES 6-12', headline 'The Summer Reading Trail', and a subhead stating ten weeks, sixty books, twenty minutes a day and a prize at the desk.
evidence.q2: 'Sign up a reader' appears twice above the fold, as the filled primary button in the hero and as the button at the right end of the nav bar.
evidence.q3: 'Three things, and none of them are homework' is a row of three equal cards (sign up in two minutes / read twenty minutes a day / come collect your prize); the brief never counts three.
evidence.q4: The right of the headline holds an annotated trail map with the numbered steps, 'Starts June 8 ends Aug 15' and '10 WEEKS - 60 BOOKS', so it carries information rather than filling space.
evidence.q5: Sign-up CTA in the hero and again as a dedicated 'Put a reader on the trail' form section, weekly book lists with week tabs, then the event calendar with a month grid and agenda, in the brief's own order.

evidence.q1: One hero region owns the first viewport: 'SUMMER READING 2026 / Wild Wonder' plus a paragraph naming ten weeks, ages 6 to 12, twenty minutes a day and real prizes.
evidence.q2: 'Sign my reader up' is the primary hero button, with 'Sign up free' also in the nav, both above the fold.
evidence.q3: The section labelled 'THREE STEPS' is a row of three equal numbered cards, and the grown-ups FAQ below is a further three-across card grid; the brief counts no threes.
evidence.q4: The right half beside the headline is a decorative scene (open book, sun, trees, owl) whose only text is an 'Always free' sticker; it is ornament, not content.
evidence.q5: How it works, prize ladder, weekly book lists with week tabs, event calendar with filters and dated entries, grown-ups FAQ, then the 'Register a reader' form: every brief-named region is present and ordered as expected.

evidence.q1: The hero occupies the first viewport down to about 83%: 'Eight weeks of reading, one stamp at a time.' with dates, ages, free, and how the stamp works.
evidence.q2: A filled 'Sign up' button sits in the hero next to 'See this week's books', and 'Sign up' is also the last nav link.
evidence.q3: Immediately under the hero is a three-column row of equal peers numbered 1-3 (sign up and pick up your log / read, then get stamped / bring your log to the party).
evidence.q4: The orange panel beside the headline shows a real reading log for 'Ada M.' with three of eight weeks stamped and a caption explaining the party ticket, so the space is content.
evidence.q5: Weekly book lists with a week strip and titles, 'What's on' as a dated branch-filtered event list, and a 'Sign up' form section, all present as separate regions in the brief's order.

evidence.q1: The teal hero dominates the first viewport with 'The summer is ten stamps long.' and a subhead explaining four books a week, stamps at any branch, and a book to keep.
evidence.q2: The red 'Join the trail' button sits directly under the hero paragraph, with 'Join' also in the nav.
evidence.q3: No three-across row anywhere: the hero grid is ten week stamps, book lists are a ten-row accordion, events are a dated list, and the join section is a two-column form plus parent questions.
evidence.q4: Beside the headline is a grid of the ten week stamps with dates and themes, week five marked 'THIS WEEK', plus an explanatory caption, all of it content.
evidence.q5: Weekly book lists, 'What's on' events by date and branch, and 'Join the trail' sign-up form with parent Q&A each occupy their own region, in the order the brief implies.

evidence.q1: The dark hero carries the proposition, 'Read eight books. Fill the card.', with eligibility, dates and live counts, and covers about three quarters of the first viewport.
evidence.q2: 'Sign up your reader' is the red primary button in the hero, and a red 'Sign up' button sits in the nav.
evidence.q3: 'How the club works' is a row of three equal columns headed STEP 1, STEP 2, STEP 3, a triplet the brief did not ask for.
evidence.q4: The panel beside the headline is a reader's card for Amara Whitcombe with four squares stamped and dated and an explanation of the mechanic.
evidence.q5: Eight weekly book lists with a week picker, 'What is on, and where' as a filtered dated event list, a 'Sign up your reader' form region, and 'For parents and carers', all present in expected order.

evidence.q1: The hero is the entire first viewport: 'Read all the way to the Summit.' plus eight weeks, eight stops, a book to keep, free for ages 6 to 12.
evidence.q2: The orange 'Sign up for the trail' button sits in the hero beside 'See this week's books'.
evidence.q3: 'How the trail works' is a row of three equal cards labelled STEP 1, STEP 2, STEP 3.
evidence.q4: The right of the headline holds a topographic trail map naming all eight numbered stops with a 'YOU ARE HERE' marker and a map legend, which is content.
evidence.q5: A dedicated 'Sign up for the trail' form, then 'Eight stops, eight book lists' with a week selector, then 'What is on this summer' as a filtered dated event list, then 'For grown-ups': the brief's regions in the brief's order.

evidence.q1: One hero region owns the first viewport, headed 'Read your way through eight weeks of summer.' with age range, what sign-up gets you, and counts of readers, events and shapes.
evidence.q2: The sign-up form itself is in the first viewport on the right, with its own 'Sign up your reader' submit button, plus the hero button and a nav button.
evidence.q3: No unearned triplet: 'How it works' runs four steps, the shape section runs eight weeks, book lists show five titles, and the parents FAQ is a two-column grid of eight questions.
evidence.q4: The space beside the headline is the working sign-up form (name, age, grown-up's email, card number, email opt-in), the most content-bearing thing that could sit there.
evidence.q5: How it works, the eight weekly shapes, 'This summer's book lists' with a week rail, 'What's on at the library' as a real month calendar, and the parents section, each its own region in expected order.

evidence.q1: The dark green hero dominates the first viewport with 'Every minute you read fills a square.' and the million-minutes-by-15-August proposition.
evidence.q2: The red 'Sign up for summer reading' button is in the hero, with 'Sign up' also the last nav link.
evidence.q3: 'What you get' is a row of three equal peers (The pin / A paperback to keep / The board and the party) that the brief never counted.
evidence.q4: Beside the headline is a live progress card, 'The Million Minute Summer', with 468,210 minutes, a 50-square board, and a note on the 2023 finish.
evidence.q5: How it works, the reading card, 'This week's books' with a week strip, 'What's on' with a July calendar and agenda, then the sign-up form and 'For grown-ups', all present and ordered sensibly.
